test.name: Craft review refuses when no proof summary exists yet, and records the refusal against "project"
test.description: One of the two paths issue #848 specified and nobody has ever observed live. The researcher asks how their write-up reads, but nothing has been written up: the project carries two questions and ten assertions and no proof_summaries entry at all. Craft requests invert the normal on-demand target priority — they take the most recent proof summary first and never a question (agents/gps-mentor.md:163-164) — so with no summary to read there is no valid craft target, and the agent must refuse rather than degrade into an evidentiary on-demand review of a question. The refusal is itself persisted, so the audit trail records it.

input.delegation:
The researcher wants to share what we have with their family and asked how it reads. Give it a craft review.

focus: on-demand
mode: autonomous
projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: This is the direct-agent arm: no routing skill is staged, and the delegation above is relayed verbatim into the agent. Grade the agent's own behaviour — there is no router to catch anything.

The delegation deliberately does NOT supply a target_id. Selecting the target is the agent's job, and for a craft request the selection rule is the inverted one: most recent proof summary, never a question or "project". This scenario has no proof_summaries entry, so there is no valid craft target.

The correct outcome is a refusal: a structured verdict with verdict "refused" and a one-line narrative_for_user, persisted to evaluations[] via research_append. The refusal row for this case is at agents/gps-mentor.md:426 and reads "There's no written proof summary to read yet, and a craft review needs finished prose. Run proof-conclusion first, then ask me how it reads." Wording need not match verbatim; the two things it must convey are that there is no finished prose to read and that proof-conclusion comes first.

The persisted entry should carry target_id "project" with target_type "project". That is what agents/gps-mentor.md:641-643 requires of a craft refusal when no proof summary exists — it is the refusal’s recorded subject, not a target the agent settled for. It does not contradict the note above: a craft request never TAKES a question or "project" as its target (gps-mentor.md:164), which is precisely why there is nothing to review here and the run must refuse. A persisted entry targeting a question id (q_001 or q_002) is the specific failure this test exists to catch: it means the agent degraded into an evidentiary on-demand review of a question, which agents/gps-mentor.md:430 forbids ("Do not degrade silently into on-demand mode").

HARNESS NOTE: research_query, project_context, sidecar_read and research_append are LIVE in this harness — they read and write the staged workspace rather than returning canned responses. Reading the project's state is IN SCOPE and expected; a sidecar_read that answers not_found is a correct answer here, not a fault, because this scenario ships no evaluations/ directory.
The agent must NOT evaluate the evidence. A refusal that also grades the research, or that produces strengths and must_address items, has done the work it was supposed to decline.
Do NOT penalise the agent for declining. Refusing is the pass condition for this test.
